questions.e: Lifting the corporate veil is permitted to prevent fraud or improper conduct (e.g. using the company to evade taxes, defraud creditors, or as a sham). Courts do not lift it merely because the business is small or has few members.

questions.subject: Companies Act
questions.q: Which clause of the Memorandum of Association defines the scope of activities a company may undertake?
questions.e: The Memorandum of Association defines the company's constitution: name, registered office, objects, liability of members, and capital clauses. The doctrine of ultra vires makes acts beyond the objects clause void.

questions.subject: Companies Act
questions.q: Regarding the Articles of Association:
o: It is registered only for public companies
It contains internal management regulations and is subordinate to the Memorandum
questions.e: The Articles of Association contain the internal regulations for management — share transfers, meetings, directors' powers. They are subordinate to the Memorandum; any conflict is resolved in favour of the Memorandum.

questions.subject: Companies Act
questions.q: Under Section 26 of the Companies Act, 2013, a prospectus:
o: It must be registered with the Registrar before being issued to the public
It may omit the company's financial information
It needs no date or authorization
It can be issued before the company's incorporation
questions.e: Section 26 prescribes the contents of a prospectus: details of the issue, the company, its directors, financial information, risk factors, and reports. A prospectus inviting public subscription must be registered with the Registrar before issue.

questions.subject: Companies Act
questions.q: Under Section 35, civil liability for misstatements in a prospectus attaches to:
o: Every director, promoter and expert who authorized the issue is liable to compensate subscribers, subject to statutory defences
No liability arises if the company is solvent
Only the merchant banker is liable
questions.e: Section 35 imposes civil liability: where a prospectus contains untrue or misleading statements, every director, promoter and expert who authorized the issue is liable to compensate subscribers who suffered loss, unless they prove withdrawal of consent or reasonable grounds for belief.

questions.subject: Companies Act
questions.q: Criminal liability under Section 34 for a prospectus arises on:
o: Any untrue or misleading statement in a material particular, or omission of a material fact
Fall in the share price after listing
questions.e: Section 34: criminal liability arises where a prospectus includes any untrue or misleading statement in a material respect, or omits any material fact — punishable with imprisonment and fine. Due diligence and reasonable belief are defences.

questions.subject: Companies Act
questions.q: Under Section 139 of the Companies Act, 2013, an individual auditor may hold office for:
o: Five consecutive years for an individual auditor
questions.e: Section 139: an individual auditor holds office for one term of five consecutive years; an audit firm for two terms of five years each, followed by a five-year cooling-off. The first auditor is appointed by the Board within 30 days of incorporation.

questions.subject: Companies Act
questions.q: Under Section 141, a person is DISQUALIFIED from appointment as auditor if he has:
o: Indebtedness to the company exceeding the prescribed limit
Being a chartered accountant in practice for two years
Residence in the same city as the company
questions.e: Section 141 disqualifies, among others, a person indebted to the company beyond the prescribed limit (Rs. 5 lakh under the Rules), a person holding securities beyond the limit, or one with a business relationship with the company.

questions.subject: Companies Act
questions.q: Under Section 143, the auditor of a company has the right to:
o: Access to books of account and vouchers at all times, and the right to seek explanations from officers
questions.e: Section 143 gives the auditor the right of access to books and records at all times, to require information and explanations from officers, and to attend general meetings and be heard on matters concerning him as auditor.

questions.subject: Companies Act
questions.q: A company needs long-term funds without diluting voting control. The instrument that creates loan capital with a fixed charge on profits is:
questions.e: Section 71: debentures may be secured or unsecured. A company issuing secured debentures must create a debenture redemption reserve and appoint debenture trustees where required; debenture interest is a charge on profits.

questions.subject: Companies Act
questions.q: For a public issue of debentures under Section 71:
o: Debenture trustees must be appointed and a trust deed executed for public issues
questions.e: Section 71 requires the appointment of debenture trustees for a public issue of debentures (and for private placements above prescribed thresholds) to protect debenture holders' interests; a trust deed must be executed.

questions.subject: Companies Act
questions.q: Which statement about debentures is correct?
o: Debenture interest is payable even if the company earns no profit
Debenture redemption is at the company's discretion always
questions.e: Debenture interest is a charge against profits — it must be paid even if the company makes no profit, unlike dividend which is an appropriation. Debenture holders are creditors, not owners.

questions.subject: Companies Act
questions.q: Under Section 135, the CSR provisions apply to a company having, in the preceding financial year:
questions.e: Section 135 applies to companies with net worth of Rs. 500 crore or more, turnover of Rs. 1,000 crore or more, or net profit of Rs. 5 crore or more in the immediately preceding financial year.

questions.subject: Companies Act
questions.q: The minimum CSR expenditure required under Section 135 is:
o: 2% of average net profits of the immediately preceding three financial years
questions.e: Section 135(5): the Board must ensure at least 2% of the average net profits of the company made during the three immediately preceding financial years is spent on CSR activities; unspent amounts have specific transfer requirements.

questions.subject: Companies Act
questions.q: CSR expenditure must be incurred on:
o: Activities listed in Schedule VII such as education, healthcare and environmental sustainability
questions.e: Schedule VII lists eligible CSR activities: eradicating hunger and poverty, education, gender equality, environmental sustainability, protection of national heritage, rural development, contributions to specified government funds, etc.

questions.subject: LLP Act
questions.q: Under the LLP Act, 2008, a Limited Liability Partnership is:
o: A body corporate with separate legal personality and limited liability of partners
An ordinary partnership with a fancy name
questions.e: An LLP is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a legal entity separate from its partners; partners' liability is limited to their agreed contribution, and the LLP can own property and sue in its own name.

questions.subject: LLP Act
questions.q: The minimum number of designated partners in an LLP is:
o: Two, with at least one resident in India
questions.e: Section 7: every LLP must have at least two designated partners, at least one of whom must be a resident in India. Designated partners are responsible for compliance and are liable for penalties for contraventions.

questions.subject: Companies Act
questions.q: Under Section 337 of the Companies Act, 2013, an offence by an officer of a company subsequently wound up includes:
o: Demanding a dividend before it is declared
Obtaining credit by false pretences with intent to defraud creditors
questions.e: Section 337 of the Companies Act, 2013 (Penalty for frauds by officers): an officer of a company which is subsequently ordered to be wound up (or passes a voluntary winding-up resolution) who has, by false pretences or any other fraud, induced any person to give credit to the company (clause a), is punishable with imprisonment of not less than one year and up to three years and a fine of not less than Rs. 1 lakh and up to Rs. 3 lakh. Note: LLP Act ss.68-69 cover electronic filing of documents and payment of additional fee, not fraud.

questions.subject: Indian Contract Act
questions.q: A person lawfully does something for another person, not intending to do so gratuitously, and such other person enjoys the benefit thereof. Under the Indian Contract Act, the latter is bound to make compensation to the former under which section?
questions.e: Section 70 imposes an obligation on a person who enjoys the benefit of a non-gratuitous act: the beneficiary must compensate the person who lawfully did the act. Section 68 covers necessaries supplied to persons incapable of contracting; Section 69 covers reimbursement when a person interested in payment pays money another is bound to pay; Section 72 covers money paid by mistake or under coercion, which must be repaid.

questions.subject: Indian Contract Act
questions.q: Money paid by mistake or under coercion must be repaid or returned. This quasi-contractual obligation is under:
questions.e: Section 70 covers obligations of a person enjoying the benefit of a non-gratuitous act; Section 72 covers money paid by mistake or under coercion, which must be repaid. Quantum meruit (as much as deserved) is the related common-law principle for part performance.

questions.subject: Indian Contract Act
questions.q: Compensation for breach of contract is NOT available for:
o: Loss naturally arising in the usual course
Loss the parties knew was likely at contracting
Remote and indirect loss not contemplated by the parties
Loss of profit on the contract itself
questions.e: Section 73's second limb: compensation for breach is not given for remote and indirect loss. The famous illustration — a carrier's delay causing loss of a lucrative government contract — is not recoverable because it was not in the parties' contemplation.

questions.subject: Indian Contract Act
questions.q: Where time is of the essence and the promisor fails to perform at the fixed time, under Section 55:
o: The promisee must perform within a reasonable time, and the contract is voidable at his option if time was of the essence
The promisee can claim double damages
questions.e: Where no time is fixed, Section 46 requires performance within a reasonable time; what is reasonable is a question of fact. Section 55 covers failure to perform at a fixed time where time is of the essence — the contract becomes voidable at the promisee's option.

questions.subject: Indices
questions.q: Cubing the decimal 0.04 gives:
questions.e: (0.04)^3 = 0.04 x 0.04 x 0.04 = 0.0016 x 0.04 = 0.000064. When raising a decimal to a power, multiply the decimals and place the point so that the total decimal places equal the sum (2 x 3 = 6).

questions.subject: Indices
questions.q: The value of sqrt(625/49) is:
questions.e: The square root of a fraction is the square root of the numerator over the square root of the denominator: sqrt(625)/sqrt(49) = 25/7.

questions.subject: Indices
questions.q: 27^(2/3) equals:
questions.e: a^(m/n) = (n-th root of a)^m. 27^(2/3) = (cube root of 27)^2 = 3^2 = 9.

questions.subject: Linear inequalities
questions.q: Solving the linear inequality 5 - 2x > -1, the values of x must satisfy:
questions.e: Bring all terms to one side: 2x - 6 < 0, so x < 3. The inequality sign reverses only when multiplying or dividing by a negative number, which does not happen here.

questions.subject: Linear inequalities
questions.q: The values of x satisfying |2x - 4| <= 6 form the interval:
questions.e: |2x - 4| <= 6 gives -6 <= 2x - 4 <= 6, i.e. -2 <= 2x <= 10, so -1 <= x <= 5. The closed interval [-1, 5] is the solution.

questions.subject: Linear inequalities
questions.q: The inequality (x - 2)(x + 3) >= 0 holds for:
questions.e: (x-2)(x+3) >= 0 holds where both factors are non-negative (x >= 2) or both non-positive (x <= -3). The parabola opens upward, so it is non-negative outside the roots.

questions.subject: Simple interest
questions.q: Rs. 8,000 is invested at 6% p.a. simple interest for 2.5 years. The interest earned is:
questions.e: Simple interest = P x r x t / 100 = 8000 x 6 x 2.5 / 100 = Rs. 1,200. Simple interest grows linearly with time, unlike compound interest.

questions.subject: Simple interest
questions.q: If Rs. 5,000 is placed at 8% per annum simple interest for three years, the interest earned equals:
questions.e: SI = 5000 x 8 x 3/100 = Rs. 1,200; amount = Rs. 6,200. At simple interest the annual charge is constant because it is always computed on the original principal.

questions.subject: Simple interest
questions.q: In how many years will Rs. 7,500 amount to Rs. 9,000 at 5% p.a. simple interest?

questions.subject: CI vs SI
questions.q: The difference between compound and simple interest on Rs. 10,000 at 10% p.a. for 3 years is:
questions.e: At 10% for 3 years: CI = 10,000 x [(1.1)^3 - 1] = 10,000 x 0.331 = Rs. 3,310; SI = 10,000 x 0.10 x 3 = Rs. 3,000. Difference = Rs. 310. The gap widens with higher rates and longer periods.

questions.subject: CI vs SI
questions.q: Rs. 20,000 is lent at 5% p.a. The excess of compound interest over simple interest for 2 years is:
questions.e: For 2 years, CI - SI = P x (r/100)^2 = 20,000 x (0.05)^2 = 20,000 x 0.0025 = Rs. 50. This shortcut works only for a two-year period.

questions.subject: CI vs SI
questions.q: Rs. 10,000 at 8% p.a. compounded half-yearly for 2 years amounts to approximately:
questions.e: Half-yearly compounding: rate per half-year = 4%, periods = 4. Amount = 10,000 x (1.04)^4 = 10,000 x 1.16986 = Rs. 11,698.56, approx Rs. 11,699. More frequent compounding raises the effective yield.

questions.subject: Annuities
questions.q: Rs. 5,000 is deposited at the end of each year for 10 years at 8% p.a. The accumulated amount is approximately:
questions.e: FV of annuity = R x [((1+i)^n - 1)/i] = 5000 x [((1.08)^10 - 1)/0.08] = 5000 x 14.4866 = Rs. 72,433. Each deposit compounds for a different remaining term.

questions.subject: Annuities
questions.q: The present value of a perpetual annual payment of Rs. 2,000 at 8% p.a. is:
questions.e: This is a perpetuity: PV = annual payment / interest rate = 2,000 / 0.08 = Rs. 25,000. A perpetuity's value is finite because distant payments are discounted almost to zero.

questions.subject: Present value
questions.q: Discounting Rs. 12,100 receivable two years hence at 10% per annum gives a present value of:
questions.e: PV = FV/(1+i)^n = 12,100/(1.1)^2 = 12,100/1.21 = Rs. 10,000. Discounting reverses compounding.

questions.subject: Present value
questions.q: Rs. 50,000 receivable after 3 years is worth today at a 12% discount rate approximately:
questions.e: PV = 50,000/(1.12)^3 = 50,000/1.4049 = Rs. 35,589 (approx). Higher discount rates and longer waits both shrink present value.

questions.subject: Progressions
questions.q: The 8th term of the geometric progression 3, 6, 12, ... is:
questions.e: In the GP 3, 6, 12, ..., a = 3 and r = 2. The n-th term = a x r^(n-1), so the 8th term = 3 x 2^7 = 3 x 128 = 384.

questions.subject: Progressions
questions.q: Adding the first six terms of the geometric series 2, 6, 18, 54, ... yields:

questions.subject: Progressions
questions.q: An infinite geometric series begins 9, 3, 1, 1/3 and continues in the same ratio. Its total is:
questions.e: Here a = 9 and r = 1/3. For |r| < 1 the infinite sum is a/(1 - r) = 9/(1 - 1/3) = 9/(2/3) = 13.5.

questions.subject: Limits
questions.q: The limit of (x^2 - 9)/(x - 3) as x tends to 3 is:
questions.e: Factorising: (x^2 - 9)/(x - 3) = (x-3)(x+3)/(x-3) = x + 3 for x != 3. As x approaches 3, the value approaches 6.

questions.subject: Limits
questions.q: The limit of sin(5x)/x as x tends to 0 is:
questions.e: sin(5x)/x = 5 x sin(5x)/(5x). Since sin(u)/u tends to 1 as u tends to 0, the limit is 5 x 1 = 5.

questions.subject: Limits
questions.q: The limit of (1 + 1/n)^n as n tends to infinity is:
questions.e: (1 + 1/n)^n tends to e (approximately 2.718) as n tends to infinity — the defining limit of the exponential constant, used in continuous compounding.

questions.subject: Logarithms
questions.q: The logarithmic equation log2(x) = 5 is solved by x equal to:
questions.e: log2(32) = 5 because 2^5 = 32. A logarithm is the exponent to which the base must be raised.

questions.subject: Logarithms
questions.q: The value of log(1000) - log(10) (base 10) is:
questions.e: log(1000) - log(10) = log(1000/10) = log(100) = 2 (base 10). The difference of logs is the log of the quotient.

questions.subject: Linear equations
questions.q: Solving 2x + 3y = 12 and x - y = 1 gives:
questions.e: From x - y = 1, x = y + 1. Substituting: 2(y+1) + 3y = 12, so 5y = 10, y = 2 and x = 3.

questions.subject: Linear equations
questions.q: The system 2x + 3y = 5 and 4x + 6y = 10 has:
questions.e: a1/a2 = 2/4 = 1/2, b1/b2 = 3/6 = 1/2, c1/c2 = 5/10 = 1/2. All three ratios equal, so the lines coincide and there are infinitely many solutions.

questions.subject: Arithmetic progression
questions.q: The sum of the first 20 natural numbers is:
questions.e: Sum of first n natural numbers = n(n+1)/2 = 20 x 21/2 = 210.

questions.subject: Arithmetic progression
questions.q: The 15th term of the arithmetic progression 5, 9, 13, ... is:
questions.e: For AP 5, 9, 13, ..., a = 5 and d = 4. The n-th term = a + (n-1)d, so the 15th term = 5 + 14 x 4 = 61.

questions.subject: Sets
questions.q: In a class, 30 students like tea, 25 like coffee, and 12 like both. The number who like at least one is:
questions.e: n(A U B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A n B) = 30 + 25 - 12 = 43. The intersection is subtracted once because it was counted twice.

questions.subject: Sets
questions.q: (A U B)' equals:
questions.e: De Morgan's law: the complement of a union is the intersection of complements, (A U B)' = A' n B'.

questions.subject: Bayes' theorem
questions.q: Urn I has 3 red and 2 black balls, Urn II has 2 red and 3 black balls. An urn is chosen with probabilities 0.6 and 0.4. A red ball is drawn. By Bayes' theorem, the probability it came from Urn I is approximately:

questions.subject: Bayes' theorem
questions.q: 1% of a population has a disease. A test is 99% sensitive and 95% specific. If a person tests positive, the probability he has the disease is approximately:

questions.subject: Regression
questions.q: If r = 0.8 and the regression coefficient of y on x is 0.5, the regression coefficient of x on y is:
questions.e: The two regression coefficients satisfy b_yx x b_xy = r^2. So b_xy = r^2/b_yx = 0.64/0.5 = 1.28.

questions.subject: Regression
questions.q: When the correlation coefficient is zero, the two regression lines are:
questions.e: If r = 0, b_yx = b_xy = 0, so the y-on-x line is horizontal (y = mean of y) and the x-on-y line is vertical (x = mean of x) — they are perpendicular.

questions.subject: Integration
questions.q: Evaluating the definite integral of 2x between the limits 0 and 1 gives:
questions.e: Integral from 0 to 1 of 2x dx = [x^2] from 0 to 1 = 1. Geometrically this is the area of a triangle with base 1 and height 2.

questions.subject: Integration
questions.q: An antiderivative of the function 3x^2 is:
questions.e: Integral of 3x^2 dx = x^3 + C, since differentiating x^3 gives 3x^2. The constant C covers the family of antiderivatives.

questions.subject: Ratio & proportion
questions.q: The duplicate ratio of 3:4 is:
questions.e: Duplicate ratio of a:b is a^2:b^2 = 9:16. The duplicate ratio compounds a ratio with itself.

questions.subject: Ratio & proportion
questions.q: The sub-duplicate ratio of 16:9 is:
questions.e: Sub-duplicate ratio of 16:9 is sqrt(16):sqrt(9) = 4:3. Triplicate would cube the terms; sub-duplicate takes square roots.

questions.subject: Combinations
questions.q: The number of ways of choosing 3 students from 10 is:
questions.e: 10C3 = 10!/(3!7!) = (10 x 9 x 8)/(3 x 2 x 1) = 120. Order of selection does not matter in combinations.

questions.subject: Combinations
questions.q: A committee of 2 men from 5 men and 2 women from 4 women can be formed in:
questions.e: 5C2 x 4C2 = 10 x 6 = 60. The choices from the two groups are independent, so the counts multiply.

questions.subject: Theory of supply
questions.q: The law of supply states that:
o: Quantity supplied rises when price rises, other things equal
Quantity supplied falls when price rises
Price and quantity supplied are unrelated
questions.e: The law of supply states that, other things remaining equal, the quantity supplied rises with price and falls when price falls — the supply curve slopes upward from left to right.

questions.subject: Theory of supply
questions.q: Supply is perfectly inelastic (a vertical supply curve) in the:
questions.e: Market period (very short run) supply is fixed — e.g. perishable goods on a given day cannot be increased however high the price. Short-run supply can vary with variable inputs; long-run supply can fully adjust.

questions.subject: Theory of supply
questions.q: Which change shifts the supply curve to the right?
o: A fall in the number of sellers
questions.e: An improvement in production technology lowers cost and shifts the supply curve rightward — more is supplied at every price. Input price rises, taxes and fewer sellers shift it left.

questions.subject: Nature & scope
questions.q: 'The government should reduce income inequality' is a statement belonging to:
questions.e: Normative economics deals with what ought to be — value judgments and policy prescriptions (e.g. 'inequality should be reduced'). Positive economics describes what is, was or will be.

questions.subject: Nature & scope
questions.q: Which of the following is a MICROECONOMIC issue?
o: The pricing of a firm's product
The national income of the country
questions.e: Microeconomics studies the behaviour of individual units — a consumer, a firm, an industry. Macroeconomy-wide aggregates like national income and general price level belong to macroeconomics.

questions.subject: Nature & scope
questions.q: The fundamental economic problem arises because of:
o: Scarcity of resources relative to wants
questions.e: Economics is a social science studying how societies allocate scarce resources among competing ends. Scarcity — unlimited wants versus limited resources — is its central problem.

questions.subject: Market structures compared
questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes monopoly from perfect competition?
o: Both earn only normal profit in the long run
Both face a horizontal demand curve
A monopolist's MR curve lies below its AR curve, while a perfect competitor's MR equals price
Both can influence the market price
questions.e: In perfect competition AR = MR = price (horizontal demand curve); in monopoly MR lies below AR because the firm must cut price on all units to sell more. Both set MC = MR for profit maximization, but only the monopolist earns long-run supernormal profit behind barriers.

questions.subject: Market structures compared
questions.q: Mutual interdependence of firms in decision-making is the hallmark of:
questions.e: Oligopoly (a few sellers) shows mutual interdependence — each firm's pricing and output decisions directly affect rivals, leading to collusion, cartels or kinked-demand price rigidity. This strategic interdependence is absent in the other structures.

questions.subject: Taxation
questions.q: Under Section 14 of the Income-tax Act, 1961, the five heads of income are:
o: Salaries; house property; business or profession; capital gains; other sources
Agriculture; salaries; business; capital gains; gifts
Direct income; indirect income; exempt income; deemed income; casual income
questions.e: Section 14 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 classifies income under five heads: salaries, income from house property, profits and gains of business or profession, capital gains, and income from other sources.

questions.subject: Taxation
questions.q: The basic condition for an individual to be 'resident' in India is stay in India during the previous year of:
questions.e: An individual is resident in India if he is in India for 182 days or more in the previous year, or 60 days in the previous year plus 365 days in the four preceding years (with relaxed thresholds for certain persons).

questions.subject: Taxation
questions.q: The maximum deduction available under Section 80C is:
questions.e: Section 80C allows deduction up to Rs. 1,50,000 for LIC premiums, PPF, ELSS, tuition fees, principal repayment of housing loan and similar specified investments and payments.

questions.subject: Taxation
questions.q: The standard deduction available to a salaried employee under the old tax regime is:
questions.e: Under the old (regular) regime, a standard deduction of Rs. 50,000 is available from salary income in place of the earlier transport and medical allowances.

questions.subject: Taxation
questions.q: Tax deducted at source on salary payments is governed by:
o: Section 192 — deduction at the average applicable rate from estimated salary income
questions.e: Section 192 requires the employer to deduct tax at source from salary at the average rate applicable to the employee's estimated total income — TDS is only a mode of collection, and the employee still files a return.

questions.subject: Audit
questions.q: The overall objectives of the independent auditor under SA-200 are:
o: To obtain reasonable assurance that financial statements are free from material misstatement and report accordingly
To guarantee the company's future profits
questions.e: SA 200 establishes the independent auditor's overall objectives: to obtain reasonable assurance that the financial statements are free from material misstatement and to report in accordance with the auditor's findings.

questions.subject: Audit
questions.q: Under SA-500, the auditor should obtain:
o: Sufficient appropriate evidence, with external evidence generally more reliable than internal
questions.e: SA 500 deals with audit evidence: the auditor must design procedures to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence. Appropriateness means relevance and reliability; external documentary evidence is generally more reliable than internal or oral evidence.

questions.subject: Audit
questions.q: The Companies (Auditor's Report) Order, 2020 requires reporting on how many clauses?
questions.e: CARO, 2020 requires the auditor to report on 21 specified clauses covering fixed assets, inventories, loans, deposits, cost records, statutory dues, fraud, and related matters for applicable companies.

questions.subject: Partnership
questions.q: A and B share profits 3:2. C is admitted with a guaranteed minimum profit of Rs. 30,000, the guarantee given by A alone. The firm's profit is Rs. 1,50,000 and the new ratio is 3:2:1. How much does A bear for the guarantee?
questions.e: C's profit share = 1,50,000 x 1/6 = Rs. 25,000, which is Rs. 5,000 short of the guaranteed Rs. 30,000. Since A alone gave the guarantee, A bears the entire shortfall of Rs. 5,000 out of his own share.

questions.subject: Tax
questions.q: Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, TDS on immovable-property transfers involving a non-resident seller is captured by:

questions.topic: Journal, Ledger & Trial Balance — the Accounting Cycle
questions.q: A journal is called the book of original entry because:
o: It is the first book maintained by every business
Transactions are recorded in it first, in chronological order, from source documents
It contains only the original vouchers
It is maintained before the ledger is opened each year
questions.e: The journal is the book of original entry because every transaction is first recorded there in date order, directly from the source document, before being posted to the ledger (the book of secondary entry).

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Journal, Ledger & Trial Balance — the Accounting Cycle
questions.q: Journalise: purchased furniture of ₹50,000 on credit from M/s Sharma & Co.
o: Purchases A/c Dr ₹50,000 — To Cash A/c ₹50,000
Furniture A/c Dr ₹50,000 — To M/s Sharma & Co. A/c ₹50,000
M/s Sharma & Co. A/c Dr ₹50,000 — To Furniture A/c ₹50,000
Furniture A/c Dr ₹50,000 — To Purchases A/c ₹50,000
questions.e: Furniture is a real account — debit what comes in. M/s Sharma & Co. is a personal account — credit the giver. So: Furniture A/c Dr ₹50,000 To M/s Sharma & Co. A/c ₹50,000. It is not 'Purchases' because furniture is an asset, not goods for resale.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Journal, Ledger & Trial Balance — the Accounting Cycle
questions.q: Which of the following errors will a trial balance NOT disclose?
o: A payment of ₹3,000 recorded only in the cash book
Two errors of ₹1,500 each that cancel each other out
questions.e: Compensating errors cancel each other, so debits still equal credits and the trial balance tallies. The other three all create a one-sided debit/credit difference (casting error, one-sided posting, short debit), so the trial balance would disagree.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Journal, Ledger & Trial Balance — the Accounting Cycle
questions.q: Commission of ₹5,000 received in cash should be journalised as:
o: Cash A/c Dr ₹5,000 — To Commission A/c ₹5,000
Commission A/c Dr ₹5,000 — To Cash A/c ₹5,000
Cash A/c Dr ₹5,000 — To Capital A/c ₹5,000
Bank A/c Dr ₹5,000 — To Commission A/c ₹5,000
questions.e: Cash is a real account — debit what comes in. Commission received is an income, a nominal account — credit all incomes and gains. So Cash A/c Dr ₹5,000 To Commission A/c ₹5,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Journal, Ledger & Trial Balance — the Accounting Cycle
questions.q: The ledger is primarily known as the book of:
o: Secondary entry and classification of accounts
questions.e: The ledger receives postings from the journal, so it is the book of secondary entry; because each account (Cash, Sales, Ram) is maintained separately, it is also the book of classification. The trial balance — not the ledger — tests arithmetical accuracy.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts — Trading, P&L & Balance Sheet
questions.q: Gross profit is calculated as:
o: Net sales minus cost of goods sold
questions.e: Gross Profit = Net Sales − Cost of Goods Sold (opening stock + net purchases + direct expenses − closing stock). Total expenses give net profit; assets minus liabilities gives capital employed.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts — Trading, P&L & Balance Sheet
questions.q: Closing stock of ₹60,000 is shown in the final accounts as:
o: Debited to Trading A/c and shown as a liability
Credited to Trading A/c and shown as a current asset
Debited to P&L A/c and shown as a fixed asset
Credited to P&L A/c and deducted from purchases
questions.e: Closing stock is credited to the Trading Account (it reduces cost of goods sold — unsold goods belong to the next period) and shown on the assets side of the Balance Sheet as a current asset. It is the classic two-place adjustment.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts — Trading, P&L & Balance Sheet
questions.q: Salaries paid ₹1,80,000; outstanding salaries at year-end ₹20,000. The P&L Account will show:
questions.e: On accrual basis, the expense for the year is paid + outstanding = ₹1,80,000 + ₹20,000 = ₹2,00,000, debited to P&L. The ₹20,000 outstanding also appears as a liability in the Balance Sheet.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts — Trading, P&L & Balance Sheet
questions.q: Net profit of ₹85,000 for the year is transferred to:
o: The debit side of the Capital Account
The credit side of the Capital Account
The debit side of the Trading Account
The assets side of the Balance Sheet
questions.e: Net profit increases the owner's claim on the business, so it is credited to the Capital Account. Drawings do the opposite — they are debited (deducted from) capital.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.topic: Final Accounts — Trading, P&L & Balance Sheet
questions.q: Which statement about the Balance Sheet is correct?
o: It is a nominal account showing profit for the year
It is a statement of financial position as on a particular date
Its debit side always exceeds its credit side
questions.e: The Balance Sheet is a position statement (not an account) showing assets, liabilities and capital as on a specific date — 'as at 31st March'. Both sides always agree; it covers accrual-based, not just cash, items.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: A machine costs ₹1,00,000, scrap value ₹10,000, useful life 10 years. Annual depreciation under SLM is:
questions.e: SLM = (Cost − Scrap) ÷ Life = (₹1,00,000 − ₹10,000) ÷ 10 = ₹90,000 ÷ 10 = ₹9,000 per year. Forgetting to deduct scrap value is the classic trap (that would wrongly give ₹10,000).

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Under the written-down-value method, the annual depreciation charge:
o: Is charged only in profitable years
questions.e: WDV applies a fixed rate to a shrinking book value, so the rupee charge falls each year (e.g. ₹10,000, then ₹9,000, then ₹8,100 on a ₹1,00,000 asset at 10%). Depreciation is charged irrespective of profits.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Cash book shows a debit balance of ₹20,000. A cheque of ₹5,000 issued has not been presented for payment. The pass book balance will be:
questions.e: The firm reduced its cash book when the cheque was issued, but the bank's pass book still shows the money until the cheque is presented. Moving from the cash book to the pass book figure, deduct unpresented cheques: ₹20,000 − ₹5,000 = ₹15,000.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Bank charges of ₹500 debited by the bank but not recorded in the cash book are treated in the BRS (starting from cash book balance) by:
o: Adding ₹500 to the cash book balance
Deducting ₹500 from the cash book balance
Ignoring it — it nets off automatically
Adding ₹500 to the pass book balance
questions.e: Bank charges reduce the bank balance, but the firm's cash book doesn't know yet. To reconcile the cash book down to the pass book figure, deduct the ₹500 from the cash book balance.

questions.subject: Accounting
questions.q: Depreciation is charged on fixed assets primarily because of the:
o: Matching concept — cost is matched against the revenue it helps earn
questions.e: Under the matching concept, the cost of an asset is spread over the periods that benefit from its use, so each year's revenue is matched with that year's share of cost. (Going concern justifies spreading it over multiple years rather than expensing at once.)

questions.subject: Business Laws
questions.topic: Indian Contract Act — Offer, Acceptance, Consideration
questions.q: An agreement made without consideration is:
o: Void, subject to the statutory exceptions
Voidable at the option of the promisor
questions.e: Section 25 lays down 'no consideration, no contract' — such agreements are void, except for the three recognised exceptions: natural love and affection (written and registered), compensation for past voluntary service, and a written promise to pay a time-barred debt.

questions.subject: Business Laws
questions.topic: Indian Contract Act — Offer, Acceptance, Consideration
questions.q: Communication of an offer is complete:
o: When the offer is posted by the offeror
When it comes to the knowledge of the person to whom it is made
When the offeror decides to make it
questions.e: Under Section 4, communication of a proposal is complete when it comes to the knowledge of the offeree. Posting completes acceptance (against the offeror), not the offer.

questions.subject: Business Laws
questions.topic: Indian Contract Act — Offer, Acceptance, Consideration
questions.q: An advertisement inviting tenders for the supply of goods is:
o: A valid offer to the public
A concluded contract with whoever responds first
questions.e: Advertisements, price lists, auction notices and tender invitations are invitations to offer — they invite others to make offers, which the advertiser may accept or reject. There is no concluded offer until a tender is submitted and accepted.

questions.subject: Business Laws
questions.topic: Indian Contract Act — Offer, Acceptance, Consideration
questions.q: A contract entered into with a minor is:
o: Valid if the minor is a beneficiary
Valid if ratified on attaining majority
questions.e: A minor lacks contractual capacity (Section 11), so the agreement is void from the beginning — void ab initio. It cannot be ratified later on attaining majority, though a minor can be a beneficiary (e.g. of a gift) and can plead minority as a shield.

questions.subject: Business Laws
questions.topic: Indian Contract Act — Offer, Acceptance, Consideration
questions.q: Which pair is correctly distinguished?
o: Coercion needs a dominant position; undue influence needs a threat
Coercion is committing or threatening an act forbidden by law; undue influence is misusing a dominant position over another's will
Fraud requires no intention to deceive; misrepresentation requires intention
Mistake of law always voids a contract; mistake of fact never does
questions.e: Coercion (Sec 15) centres on threat of an unlawful act and can come from anyone; undue influence (Sec 16) centres on a relationship of dominance (doctor–patient, trustee–beneficiary) misused to obtain an unfair advantage. Fraud needs intent to deceive; misrepresentation is an innocent false statement.

questions.subject: Business Laws
questions.topic: Sale of Goods Act & LLP Basics
questions.q: A 'condition' under the Sale of Goods Act, 1930 is:
o: A stipulation collateral to the main purpose of the contract
A stipulation essential to the main purpose of the contract
Any term agreed orally between the parties
A term implied only by trade custom
questions.e: Section 12(2): a condition is essential to the main purpose, so its breach entitles the buyer to repudiate the contract. A warranty (Sec 12(3)) is merely collateral — breach gives damages only.

questions.subject: Business Laws
questions.topic: Sale of Goods Act & LLP Basics
questions.q: The unpaid seller's right of stoppage in transit is available when:
o: The buyer delays payment by a few days
The buyer has become insolvent and the goods are still with the carrier
The goods have already reached the buyer
The seller simply changes his mind
questions.e: Stoppage in transit lets an unpaid seller resume possession of goods in the hands of a carrier/transporter, and it arises specifically when the buyer becomes insolvent. Once the buyer takes delivery, only the personal remedies (suit for price/damages) remain.

questions.subject: Business Laws
questions.topic: Sale of Goods Act & LLP Basics
questions.q: Which statement about an LLP is correct?
o: It has no separate legal personality from its partners
Partners' liability is limited to their agreed contribution and the LLP is a body corporate
It must have at least seven partners
A partner is automatically liable for every other partner's wrongful acts
questions.e: An LLP is a body corporate with perpetual succession and separate legal personality; partners' liability is limited to the agreed contribution. Minimum two partners (no maximum); partners are agents of the LLP, not of each other.

questions.subject: Business Laws
questions.topic: Sale of Goods Act & LLP Basics
questions.q: 'Caveat emptor' means:
o: Let the buyer beware — he must examine the goods himself
The seller guarantees fitness for all purposes
Risk always stays with the seller
questions.e: Caveat emptor ('let the buyer beware') is the starting rule: the buyer must satisfy himself about quality and fitness. It is displaced by exceptions — sale by description, sale by sample, fitness for a stated purpose relied upon, and merchantable quality.

questions.subject: Business Laws
questions.topic: Sale of Goods Act & LLP Basics
questions.q: A contract for the sale of specific goods that have perished before the contract is made is:
questions.e: Where specific goods have perished (without the seller's knowledge) before the contract, the contract is void. If goods perish after agreement but before risk passes, the agreement is avoided — both turn on the goods not existing.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.q: Simple interest on ₹10,000 at 10% per annum for 3 years is:
questions.e: SI = PRT/100 = 10,000 × 10 × 3 ÷ 100 = ₹3,000. (₹3,310 would be the compound interest — a common distractor.) Amount = ₹13,000.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.q: Compound interest on ₹8,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years is:
questions.e: Amount = 8,000 × (1.10)² = 8,000 × 1.21 = ₹9,680. CI = 9,680 − 8,000 = ₹1,680. Equivalently: SI would be ₹1,600, and the 2-year CI−SI shortcut gives 8,000 × (0.10)² = ₹80 extra → ₹1,680.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.q: If a:b = 3:4 and b:c = 2:5, then a:c equals:
questions.e: Make b common: b is 4 in the first ratio and 2 in the second — multiply the second by 2 to get b:c = 4:10. Then a:b:c = 3:4:10, so a:c = 3:10.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.q: Two dice are thrown. The probability that the sum is 9 is:
questions.e: Total outcomes = 36. Favourable: (3,6), (4,5), (5,4), (6,3) — 4 outcomes. P = 4/36 = 1/9. (Sum 7 is the most likely at 6/36; 9 is less likely — don't confuse them.)

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.q: For the data 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, the mean and median are:
questions.e: Mean = (5+7+9+11+13) ÷ 5 = 45 ÷ 5 = 9. The data is already ordered with 5 values, so the median is the 3rd value = 9. For symmetric data like this, mean equals median.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.q: P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.5, with A and B independent. P(both A and B) equals:
questions.e: For independent events, the multiplication rule gives P(A∩B) = P(A) × P(B) = 0.4 × 0.5 = 0.2. (0.9 would be the addition without overlap — wrong rule for 'and'.)

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.q: The number of ways to choose a committee of 3 from 10 people is:
questions.e: Order doesn't matter in a committee, so use combinations: ¹⁰C₃ = 10! ÷ (3! × 7!) = (10 × 9 × 8) ÷ 6 = 120. (720 is ¹⁰P₃ — the permutation answer, the classic trap.)

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.q: If every observation in a dataset is multiplied by 3, the standard deviation:
questions.e: Standard deviation scales with the data: multiplying every value by k multiplies the SD by |k| (here 3). Variance would be multiplied by k² = 9 — don't confuse the two. Adding a constant leaves SD unchanged.

questions.subject: Business Economics
questions.q: The law of demand states that, other things remaining equal:
o: Quantity demanded rises as price rises
Quantity demanded falls as price rises
Supply equals demand at all prices
questions.e: The law of demand asserts an inverse price–quantity relationship, ceteris paribus. The 'other things equal' qualifier is essential — income, tastes and related-goods prices are held constant.

questions.subject: Business Economics
questions.q: Price rises by 10% and quantity demanded falls by 20%. The price elasticity of demand is:
questions.e: Ed = %ΔQ ÷ %ΔP = 20 ÷ 10 = 2 (absolute value). Since 2 > 1, demand is elastic — quantity is highly responsive, so a price cut would raise total revenue here.

questions.subject: Business Economics
questions.q: A Giffen good is one for which:
o: Demand rises as price rises, violating the law of demand
Income elasticity is positive and large
questions.e: A Giffen good is a strongly inferior staple (the textbook example: potatoes for poor households) where the income effect of a price rise outweighs the substitution effect, so quantity demanded rises with price — the exception that proves the law of demand.

questions.subject: Business Economics
questions.q: Market equilibrium occurs at the point where:
questions.e: Equilibrium is the price–quantity pair where the demand and supply curves intersect — quantity demanded equals quantity supplied, so there is neither shortage nor surplus.

questions.subject: Business Economics
questions.q: An increase in consumer income will shift the demand curve for a normal good:
o: It causes movement along the curve instead
questions.e: Higher income lets consumers buy more at every price, so the whole demand curve shifts rightward (increase in demand). A price change would instead cause movement along the curve; income changes shift it.

questions.subject: Business Economics
questions.q: In perfect competition, an individual firm is:
o: A price taker facing a perfectly elastic demand curve
Able to earn supernormal profits in the long run
questions.e: A perfect competitor is too small to influence price, so it takes the market price and faces a horizontal (perfectly elastic) demand curve. Free entry wipes out supernormal profits in the long run.

questions.subject: Business Economics
questions.q: If GDP is ₹200 lakh crore and depreciation is ₹20 lakh crore, NDP equals:
questions.e: NDP = GDP − depreciation (consumption of fixed capital) = 200 − 20 = ₹180 lakh crore. 'Net' always means 'after deducting depreciation'.

questions.subject: Business Economics
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT included in national income?
questions.e: National income counts current production only. A second-hand sale merely transfers an existing asset — no new production occurs. Wages, rent and interest are factor payments for current productive services.

questions.subject: Business Economics
questions.q: The distinguishing feature of oligopoly is:
o: Interdependence among the few sellers in pricing decisions
questions.e: With few sellers, each firm's price or output move changes rivals' outcomes, so decisions are strategically interdependent — producing kinked-demand price rigidity and heavy non-price (advertising) competition.

questions.subject: Business Economics
questions.q: Real GDP differs from nominal GDP because real GDP:
o: Is measured at base-year prices, removing inflation
questions.e: Real GDP values output at constant base-year prices, so its growth reflects genuine output growth. Nominal GDP uses current prices, mixing output growth with price rises — the GDP deflator bridges the two.

questions.subject: Inter Bridge
questions.topic: Cost Accounting Basics & GST Concept Framework
questions.q: Prime cost consists of:
o: Direct material + direct labour + direct expenses
questions.e: Prime cost = direct material + direct labour + direct expenses — all costs directly traceable to the unit. Adding factory overheads gives works cost; the fixed/variable split is a behavioural classification, not the prime-cost build-up.

questions.subject: Inter Bridge
questions.topic: Cost Accounting Basics & GST Concept Framework
questions.q: Annual usage 10,000 units, ordering cost ₹100 per order, carrying cost ₹2 per unit per annum. EOQ is:
questions.e: EOQ = √(2AO/C) = √(2 × 10,000 × 100 ÷ 2) = √1,000,000 = 1,000 units. At this quantity, total ordering cost equals total carrying cost — the minimum total inventory cost point.

questions.subject: Inter Bridge
questions.topic: Cost Accounting Basics & GST Concept Framework
questions.q: Lubricants used to maintain factory machines are classified as:
questions.e: Lubricants can't be traced to any single unit of output, so they're indirect material — part of factory overheads. Direct material must physically enter and be traceable to the product (steel in a bike).

questions.subject: Inter Bridge
questions.topic: Cost Accounting Basics & GST Concept Framework
questions.q: A supply of goods from Maharashtra to Karnataka attracts:
o: No GST — inter-state supplies are exempt
questions.e: Inter-state supplies attract IGST (collected by the Centre, with the destination state's share settled thereafter). CGST + SGST applies only to intra-state supplies. GST is destination-based, so Karnataka is where the tax ultimately belongs.

questions.subject: Inter Bridge
questions.topic: Cost Accounting Basics & GST Concept Framework
questions.q: The input tax credit (ITC) mechanism primarily ensures:
o: Exporters pay no tax at all
Tax paid on inputs is set off against output tax, removing cascading
Small businesses are exempt from registration
GST rates stay uniform across states
questions.e: ITC lets each business deduct the GST already paid on its inputs from the GST it collects on outputs, so tax falls only on the value added at each stage — the end of 'tax on tax' (cascading) that plagued the earlier regime.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: A trader's trial balance shows total debits exceeding total credits by ₹4,500. The difference should be:
o: Written off to the P&L Account
Placed to the credit of a Suspense Account
Placed to the debit of a Suspense Account
questions.e: Debits exceed credits by ₹4,500, so ₹4,500 must be placed on the credit side to make the trial balance agree — i.e. credited to a Suspense Account — until the error is traced. (If credits had exceeded debits, the suspense entry would be a debit.)

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: Rent of ₹24,000 paid for the year includes ₹4,000 relating to the next year. The P&L Account will show rent of:
questions.e: Only the current year's expense belongs in P&L: ₹24,000 − ₹4,000 (prepaid) = ₹20,000. The ₹4,000 prepaid rent appears as a current asset in the Balance Sheet.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: Under Section 2(h) of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, a 'contract' is:
o: Every promise made between two persons
Any written document signed by parties
questions.e: Section 2(h) defines a contract as an agreement enforceable by law. A bare promise or an agreement without consideration (and outside the exceptions) is not enforceable, hence not a contract.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: Goods worth ₹30,000 are destroyed by fire after sale but before delivery, with risk not yet passed to the buyer. The loss falls on:
questions.e: Risk prima facie passes with property. If property/risk had not yet passed to the buyer when the goods perished, the seller bears the loss — 'res perit domino' (the thing perishes for its owner).

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: ₹12,000 invested at 8% p.a. simple interest will double in:
questions.e: To double, interest must equal principal: P = PRT/100 → T = 100/R = 100/8 = 12.5 years. Check: 12,000 × 8 × 12.5 ÷ 100 = ₹12,000 interest.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: A bag contains 4 red and 6 black balls. One ball is drawn at random. P(red) is:
questions.e: P = favourable ÷ total = 4 ÷ 10 = 2/5. (4/6 is not a probability here — the denominator must be all 10 balls.)

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: If the price of a commodity falls and total expenditure on it rises, demand is:
questions.e: When a price fall raises total revenue (expenditure), quantity has risen proportionately more than price fell — |Ed| > 1, i.e. elastic demand. This is the revenue test for elasticity.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: Which market structure has a single seller of a product with no close substitutes?
questions.e: Monopoly = one seller, unique product, very high entry barriers — the seller is the price maker. Oligopoly has few sellers; monopolistic competition has many sellers of differentiated products.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: Depreciation for the year on machinery (WDV ₹80,000, rate 10%) is:
questions.e: WDV method: depreciation = book value × rate = ₹80,000 × 10% = ₹8,000 for the year. Next year's charge will be on ₹72,000.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: A cheque of ₹7,500 deposited into the bank was not cleared by 31st March. Starting from the cash book (Dr) balance, the BRS will:
questions.e: The firm added the deposit to its cash book, but the bank hasn't collected it yet, so the cash book is higher than the pass book by ₹7,500. Moving from the cash book balance down to the pass book figure, deduct the ₹7,500.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: An offer lapses if it is not accepted within:
o: A reasonable time or the time prescribed
questions.e: An offer must be accepted within the time prescribed in it, or within a reasonable time if none is prescribed — what is reasonable depends on the circumstances. There is no fixed statutory period like 7 or 30 days.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: A partner's liability in an LLP is:
o: Limited to the partner's agreed contribution
Joint and several for all LLP debts
questions.e: LLP partners enjoy limited liability — each partner's liability is capped at the agreed contribution. The LLP itself, as a body corporate, is liable for its own obligations.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: The compound amount of ₹5,000 at 12% p.a. compounded half-yearly for 1 year is:
questions.e: Half-yearly: rate per period = 6%, periods = 2. Amount = 5,000 × (1.06)² = 5,000 × 1.1236 = ₹5,618. (₹5,600 is the annual-compounding figure — the trap.)

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: The median of 12, 8, 20, 16, 10 is:
questions.e: Order the data: 8, 10, 12, 16, 20. The middle (3rd) value is 12. (13.2 is the mean — a common mix-up.)

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: An inferior good's income elasticity of demand is:
questions.e: Income elasticity = %ΔQ ÷ %Δincome. For inferior goods, quantity falls as income rises, so the ratio is negative. Normal goods have positive income elasticity.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: GNP exceeds GDP when:
o: Net factor income from abroad is positive
questions.e: GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad. So GNP > GDP exactly when residents earn more abroad than foreigners earn domestically (positive net factor income).

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: Wages paid ₹60,000 plus outstanding wages ₹6,000 appear in final accounts as:
o: ₹60,000 in P&L; nothing in Balance Sheet
₹66,000 in P&L (Dr) and ₹6,000 as a liability
₹54,000 in P&L and ₹6,000 as an asset
questions.e: Wages are an indirect expense: P&L debit = paid + outstanding = ₹66,000. The ₹6,000 outstanding is also shown as a current liability in the Balance Sheet.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: A minor's agreement is:
questions.e: Agreements with minors are void ab initio for want of capacity (Section 11). (A supplier of necessaries can claim against the minor's property, but that is a quasi-contractual claim, not enforcement of the agreement.)

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: If a:b = 2:3, the duplicate ratio is:
questions.e: Duplicate ratio = a²:b² = 4:9. (8:27 is the triplicate ratio — the distractor.)

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: P(A) = 0.3, P(B) = 0.4, A and B mutually exclusive. P(A or B) is:
questions.e: Mutually exclusive means P(A∩B) = 0, so the addition rule collapses: P(A∪B) = 0.3 + 0.4 = 0.7. (0.12 is the multiplication — wrong rule for 'or'.)

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: A rightward shift of the supply curve is caused by:
o: A rise in the good's own price
A rise in the price of a substitute
questions.e: Lower input costs let firms supply more at every price — the supply curve shifts right (increase in supply). A change in the good's own price causes movement along the curve; income shifts demand, not supply.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: Transfer payments (e.g. scholarships, pensions) are:
o: Included in national income at market price
Excluded — they are not payments for current production
Included only if paid by the government
Included in GDP but not in NNP
questions.e: National income counts factor payments for current productive services. Transfer payments are unilateral — no production in return — so they are excluded regardless of who pays them.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: Which cost is a fixed cost?
questions.e: Factory rent is constant in total within the relevant range — it does not change with output. The other three vary directly with production and are variable costs.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: Input tax credit is available to:
o: A registered dealer on tax paid on business inputs, set off against output tax
questions.e: ITC is the GST chain mechanism: a registered person sets off GST paid on inputs (purchases) against GST collected on outputs (sales). Final consumers bear the tax and claim no credit.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: Sales ₹4,00,000; opening stock ₹40,000; purchases ₹2,40,000; direct expenses ₹20,000; closing stock ₹60,000. Gross profit is:

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: Cash withdrawn from bank for office use ₹10,000 is recorded as:
o: Cash A/c Dr — To Bank A/c
Bank A/c Dr — To Cash A/c
Drawings A/c Dr — To Bank A/c
Office Expenses A/c Dr — To Cash A/c
questions.e: Contra entry: cash (real account) comes in — debit Cash; bank balance goes out — credit Bank. It is not drawings (that's for personal use) and not an expense yet.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: Communication of acceptance is complete against the offeror when:
o: The letter of acceptance is posted
questions.e: Section 4: acceptance is complete against the proposer when it is put in transmission beyond the acceptor's recall — e.g. posted. Against the acceptor, it completes only when it reaches the offeror's knowledge.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: Breach of warranty entitles the buyer to:
o: Reject the goods and repudiate the contract
questions.e: Warranty is collateral to the main purpose (Sec 12(3)) — breach gives damages only. Rejection/repudiation is the remedy for breach of condition.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: ₹9,000 amounts to ₹11,070 in 3 years at simple interest. The rate is:

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: ⁸P₂ equals:
questions.e: ⁸P₂ = 8 × 7 = 56 (order matters). The combination ⁸C₂ = 28 — pick permutation only when arrangement/order counts.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: If demand is perfectly inelastic, the demand curve is:
questions.e: Perfectly inelastic means quantity does not respond to price at all — the curve is vertical. (Perfectly elastic is the horizontal one — don't swap them.)

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: In the long run, a perfectly competitive firm earns:
questions.e: Free entry and exit compete away supernormal profits: new firms enter when profits are supernormal, driving price down until only normal profits remain. Losses likewise trigger exit.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: Direct expenses of a factory for the month total ₹18,000; direct wages ₹1,50,000. Using direct wages as base, the absorption rate for direct-expense-type overheads is:
questions.e: Absorption rate = overheads ÷ base = 18,000 ÷ 1,50,000 = 0.12 = 12% of direct wages. Each job then absorbs 12% of its direct wages as this overhead.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of 'other things equal' failing, so the demand curve shifts rather than moves?
o: Consumer tastes shift towards the good
questions.e: Tastes are a non-price determinant — a shift towards the good moves the whole demand curve rightward. Price changes (including discounts) cause movement along the fixed curve.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: A time-barred debt of ₹25,000 is promised in writing by the debtor. The promise is:
o: Valid — an exception to 'no consideration, no contract'
questions.e: Section 25(3): a promise in writing, signed, to pay a time-barred debt is enforceable — one of the three exceptions to the no-consideration rule, alongside registered natural-love-and-affection agreements and past voluntary service.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: The standard deviation of the values 7, 7, 7, 7 is:
questions.e: All values equal the mean, so every deviation is zero — SD = 0. Any constant dataset has zero spread.

questions.e: Tea and coffee are substitutes: a rise in coffee's price raises tea's quantity demanded, so %ΔQ(tea) ÷ %ΔP(coffee) > 0 — positive cross elasticity. Complements (car–petrol) show negative cross elasticity.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: EOQ rises when:
questions.e: EOQ = √(2AO/C): it rises with A (annual usage) and O (ordering cost), and falls with C (carrying cost). Bigger annual demand justifies bigger, fewer orders.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: Paid wages ₹45,000 in cash. The journal entry is:
o: Cash A/c Dr ₹45,000 — To Wages A/c ₹45,000
Wages A/c Dr ₹45,000 — To Cash A/c ₹45,000
Wages A/c Dr ₹45,000 — To Capital A/c ₹45,000
Cash A/c Dr ₹45,000 — To Capital A/c ₹45,000
questions.e: Wages is a nominal account (expense) — debit all expenses. Cash (real account) goes out — credit what goes out. So Wages A/c Dr ₹45,000 To Cash A/c ₹45,000.

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: A trial balance will definitely disagree if:

The sales book is overcast by ₹1,000
Office furniture is debited to Office Expenses

questions.subject: Mock Paper

Goods are sold by description and don't correspond to it

Rightward — cars and petrol are complements

questions.subject: Mock Paper
questions.q: Acceptance of an offer must be:

questions.subject: Mock Paper

questions.subject: Mock Paper

questions.subject: Mock Paper

Higher prices induce producers to offer more, ceteris paribus

questions.subject: Mock Paper

questions.e: Leakages withdraw from the flow: saving (S), taxes (T), imports (M). Injections add to it: investment (I), government spending (G), exports (X). Equilibrium: S + T + M = I + G + X.

Absorbed overheads were less than actual overheads

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI October 2026: decoding the rate table
capsules.body: The MPC's 7 October 2026 decision: repo 5.50% (up 25 bps, first hike since February 2023, unanimous); SDF 5.25%; MSF and Bank Rate 5.75%; CRR 3.00%; SLR 18.00%. In the LAF corridor, the SDF is the floor and the MSF/Bank Rate the ceiling, with the repo as the policy rate in the middle. The stance moved from 'neutral' to 'calibrated tightening' on a 4-2 vote - meaning rate cuts are off the table; the next move can only be a hike or a pause. The RBI expects headline CPI to average almost 5.8% over the next three quarters (drivers: crude at $114-116/barrel amid West Asia war escalation; 13% monsoon deficit under El Nino; August CPI 4.82%), and projects 5.2% CPI with 7.1% real GDP growth for FY27.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: FPI tax change via ordinance (October 2026)
capsules.body: The Income-tax Amendment Ordinance, 2026 exempts FPI investments in government securities from tax on interest and capital gains with effect from 1 April 2026. ASSOCHAM welcomed it on 19 October 2026, saying the forward-looking move will attract stable, long-term capital from pension funds, sovereign wealth funds and insurance companies. It also welcomed the Finance Minister's 13 October remarks at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum on consulting investors on long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax and securities transaction tax (STT) as part of Union Budget 2027-28 consultations, calling it a reassurance for global investors.

capsules.subject: Income Tax
capsules.title: CBDT extends AY 2026-27 audit and ITR deadlines; SAKSHAM NUDGE
capsules.body: CBDT Circular No. 07/2026 (28 September 2026): the tax audit report (Form 3CA/3CB with Form 3CD) for AY 2026-27 in specified non-transfer-pricing cases is extended from 30 September to 21 October 2026; the corresponding ITR deadline moves from 31 October to 21 November 2026. This is not a blanket extension - transfer-pricing cases keep their 31 October (Form 3CEB) and 30 November (ITR) dates. The Income Tax Department's SAKSHAM NUDGE campaign (Non-Intrusive Usage of Data to Guide and Enable) has reminded about 12,000 tax professionals who had filed fewer than 50% of their AY 2026-27 audit reports compared with the previous financial year; over 19.5 lakh audit reports have already been filed. Missing the deadline can attract a Section 271B penalty up to Rs 1,50,000. - Verified: 20 Oct 2026

capsules.subject: Regulatory Updates
capsules.title: FEMA (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026 — effective 1 Oct 2026
capsules.body: The RBI notified the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026, effective 1 October 2026. Key compliance points for CAs: AD banks must upload export/import data in EDPMS/IDPMS within 5 working days for non-EDI ports; timeline for realisation and repatriation of export proceeds is 15 months, extended to 18 months for exports invoiced or settled in Indian rupees; self-declaration permitted for closure of export-monitoring entries up to Rs 10 lakh.

capsules.subject: Regulatory Updates
capsules.title: Section 42(1) RBI Act: minimum daily CRR maintenance raised to 99%
capsules.body: The RBI (notification dated 9 Oct 2026, under Section 42(1) of the RBI Act, 1934) raised the minimum daily CRR maintenance for scheduled banks from 90% to 99%, effective the reporting fortnight beginning 16 October 2026. The prescribed CRR rate is unchanged at 3% and average compliance over the fortnight continues. Rationale: managing surplus system liquidity (~Rs 4 lakh crore) amid the shift to calibrated tightening.

capsules.subject: Regulatory Updates
capsules.title: UCB prudential norms: unsecured-advances ceiling to 20%; Mission-SAKSHAM
capsules.body: The RBI proposed doubling the aggregate ceiling on unsecured advances for UCBs from 10% to 20% of total assets (from 1 Oct 2026): beyond-ceiling unsecured advances allowed only for priority-sector-eligible loans up to Rs 50,000 per borrower; nominal-member consumer-durable lending proposed at Rs 2.5 lakh per borrower; maximum unsecured loan limits of Rs 5 lakh (Tier-1), Rs 7.5 lakh (Tier-2), Rs 10 lakh (Tier-3/4); housing-loan tenor and moratorium deregulated for Tier-3 and Tier-4 UCBs. The RBI also announced Mission-SAKSHAM to train over 1.4 lakh UCB staff.

capsules.subject: Regulatory Updates
capsules.title: RBI October 2026 policy: repo to 5.50% — first hike since Feb 2023
capsules.body: The MPC (5-7 Oct 2026, Governor Sanjay Malhotra) raised the repo rate 25 bps to 5.50% — the first hike since February 2023 — and shifted the stance to 'calibrated tightening' (SDF 5.25%; MSF and Bank Rate 5.75%). FY27 inflation forecast raised to 5.2% on August CPI of 4.82% and crude above $100/barrel; Q1 FY27 GDP growth 7.8%. For CAs: expect upward transmission to lending rates (home, vehicle, personal loans) and firming deposit rates over the coming weeks.

oneliners.subject: Current Affairs
oneliners.text: India's September 2026 retail inflation climbed to 5.54%, driven by food price spikes - keeping monetary authorities vigilant (Oct 2026).

oneliners.subject: Current affairs
oneliners.text: The SC on 15 Oct 2026 upheld the quashing of Yes Bank's ₹8,415 crore AT1 bond write-off (Yes Bank v Axis Trusteeship), affirming the Bombay HC judgment of 20 Jan 2023.

oneliners.text: Jio showcased AI smart glasses at India Mobile Congress 2026 with 'Scan & Pay' voice-controlled UPI payments and UPI Circle support (₹5,000 per transaction, ₹15,000 monthly limit).

oneliners.text: India's trade deficit with China crossed $100 billion in 2026 (customs data reported 15 October 2026).

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: CPI retail inflation: 5.54% in September 2026 — a 23-month high (from 4.83% in August).

oneliners.subject: ICAI updates
oneliners.text: The January 2027 CA attempt covers Foundation and Intermediate (Group I on 2, 4, 6 January; Group II on 8, 10, 12 January), with exams also held at overseas centres in Bahrain, Dubai and Kathmandu.

oneliners.subject: ICAI updates
oneliners.text: Under the ICAI new scheme, a candidate must score at least 40% in each paper and 50% in aggregate across a group to pass.

oneliners.subject: Current affairs
oneliners.text: ICAI CA Final November 2026: Group I on 2, 4, 6 November; Group II on 9, 11, 13 November; admit cards about 15 days before.

oneliners.subject: Current affairs
oneliners.text: CA Foundation September 2026 exams were held 2, 5, 7 and 9 September; results expected in the first week of November 2026.

oneliners.subject: Current affairs
oneliners.text: RBI raised the repo rate to 5.50% on 7 October 2026 — borrowing costs rise across the economy.

oneliners.subject: Current Affairs
oneliners.text: ICAI released the CA Final November 2026 admit cards on 17-18 October 2026 at eservices.icai.org; no physical copies are sent by post.

oneliners.subject: Current Affairs
oneliners.text: CA Final November 2026: Group I on 2, 4 and 6 November; Group II on 9, 11 and 13 November (papers 1-5 from 2 PM to 5 PM; Paper 6 from 2 PM to 6 PM).

oneliners.subject: Current Affairs
oneliners.text: CA Final November 2026 papers: Financial Reporting, Advanced Financial Management, Advanced Auditing & Professional Ethics, Direct Tax Laws & International Taxation, Indirect Tax Laws, and Integrated Business Solutions.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: RBI October 2026 policy (7 October, Governor Sanjay Malhotra): repo 5.50% (+25 bps, first hike since February 2023), SDF 5.25%, MSF and Bank Rate 5.75%; stance 'calibrated tightening' (4-2 vote); FY27 CPI forecast 5.2%, real GDP growth 7.1%; CRR stays 3.00%, SLR 18.00%.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: Income-tax Amendment Ordinance, 2026: FPI investments in government securities are exempt from tax on interest and capital gains from 1 April 2026 (welcomed by ASSOCHAM on 19 October 2026).

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: Ethanol FY27 tender (supply year Nov 2026-Oct 2027): no sugar-based ethanol; maize incentive cut; grain-based feedstocks to carry the E20 blending programme.

oneliners.subject: GST
oneliners.text: October 2026 GST calendar: GSTR-1 due 11 October, CMP-08 on 18 October, GSTR-3B/GSTR-5/GSTR-5A on 20 October, quarterly GSTR-3B under QRMP on 22/24 October, PMT-06 on 25 October, GSTR-11 (UIN holders) on 28 October. - Verified: 20 Oct 2026

oneliners.subject: Exam Updates
oneliners.text: ICAI CA Final Nov 2026 admit card released (17-18 Oct 2026) at eservices.icai.org; exams 2-13 Nov 2026 - Group I (Nov 2, 4, 6), Group II (Nov 9, 11, 13); papers 1-5 at 2-5 PM, Paper 6 at 2-6 PM (open book); reading time from 1:45 PM; no admit cards by post. (21 Oct 2026)

oneliners.subject: Exam Updates
oneliners.text: Withheld CA admit cards are often due to incomplete Advanced ICITSS or pending self-paced online modules; candidates with unclear photo/signature should carry an attested photo and signature letter with a valid govt photo ID. (21 Oct 2026)

oneliners.subject: ICAI Exams
oneliners.text: 21 Oct 2026: ICAI January 2027 exams — Inter Group I (2, 4, 6 Jan), Group II (8, 10, 12 Jan), Foundation (3, 5, 7, 9 Jan); forms 3–16 Nov 2026 on eservices.icai.org.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: 21 Oct 2026: RBI's FY27 GDP forecast raised to 7.1% (from 6.7%); CPI inflation forecast for 2026–27 raised to 5.2%.
